script.hook: A new study just confirmed it — the more zero-calorie drinks you have, the hungrier you get.
body: They tested 75 people. When participants consumed a zero-calorie sweetener, hunger signals in the brain actually fired stronger — not weaker.
Blood flow in the hypothalamus spiked higher than it did with real sugar.
And the effect was strongest in people with obesity. The higher their BMI, the more intensely the sweetener triggered their appetite.
script.closer: Your brain never bought the zero-calorie story.

metadata.title: 🧠 Diet drinks make you hungrier. Science proved it. #TodaysPaper
metadata.description:
A Nature Metabolism study found that zero-calorie sweeteners activate hunger signals in the brain more strongly than real sugar — and the effect is worst in people with obesity.

📄 Paper Source
Title: Non-caloric sweetener effects on brain appetite regulation in individuals across varying body weights
Authors: Chakravartti SP et al.
Journal: Nature Metabolism (2025)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-025-01227-8
Peer-reviewed: ✅

Key finding: Randomized double-blind crossover trial in 75 adults. Sucralose triggered greater hypothalamic blood flow and hunger signaling than real sugar. The effect was most pronounced in individuals with obesity, with a clear dose-response relationship to BMI.

─
